name: slot-watch
goal: report which of today's time slots are actually bookable
schema: see ../../references/recipe-schema.md — this file is emitted FROM, never executed

recorded.how: drove it once over CDP on a throwaway Chrome, then diffed the three fixture states

observed: Slot buttons are injected ~400 ms after load by an inline script; a read at t=0 sees 'loading…'.
Button text is the time and is IDENTICAL whether or not the slot is bookable. Truth is data-available="true" and :not([disabled]).
The page fetches /api/slots with a one-shot x-slot-token minted into <meta name=slot-token>. Re-minting per run works; replaying a captured token 403s.
An #emptyBanner element states the genuine no-slots case — it exists only on variant v1.

tier.why: the page's own JSON call answers the whole question; 182 ms vs 1401 ms for the DOM path
tier.fallbackWhen: the token mint stops matching, the API shape changes, or the answer needs anything the JSON does not carry

steps.note: one-shot; must be re-minted every run

domSteps.waitFor: either .slot exists OR #emptyBanner is visible — never wait on the good outcome alone, or 'no slots' arrives as a timeout

domSteps.note: selector candidates in order of durability: structural anchor first, recorded class second, the class it was renamed to third

positive.test: any extracted row has available === true

negative.test: rows exist but none available, OR #emptyBanner visible

canary.means: the page rendered at all; distinguishes a moved element from a dead site

output.contract: one JSON object on stdout, exit 0 — every backend emits identical bytes so the bench can diff them

budget.note: the drift case costs the full timeout — it is the slowest path, not the fastest

money.note: read-only workflow; nothing here can spend

verify.mustFail: flip the fixture to variant=v2 and confirm the DOM backends say drift, not none
